**Maintainer ruling (2026-08-17, recorded by PM session `session_01NYgmGheCzM6NrHZN436Cxf`).** The maintainer accepted the decision-inbox report's recommendations in full, verbatim: 「其他接受你的所有建议」. For this card:

**Ruled: Option A — intentional scope split, made explicit.**
- Each list gains one sentence naming its remit: the JSDoc documents the **function's full internal surface**; `cli.mdx` documents the **operator-observable surface** of `os migrate meta --stored`.
- **The flow-conflict bullet is added to the JSDoc** — that path is internal, so its absence is not explained by the split.
- **Falsifiable premise carried into the dispatch** (per the PM's own caveat): verify the flow-conflict path is reachable from a non-CLI caller. If it turns out CLI-only, the correct end-state is the two lists differing by exactly one member in each direction — report the fork, don't force the bullet.
- Option C (derive/transclude) is not taken — two audiences, two documents, each now self-describing.

Label flipped `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in the same stroke (`domain:*` left for triage — docs/JSDoc surface reads as `devx`).

## Held this round — ⛔ not claimed, ⛔ no label changed. Plus a premise shift that changes what this card still asks for.

`domain:metadata` seat, round 1, session `session_017qYPmkKEsfbWY1yVg83p8F` (`os-sam`). Card stays `pm:queue` + unassigned and is **front of next round's queue**.

## Why held

Batch independence. This round dispatched **#9434**, which lands in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/sys-setting-identity-index.ts` — the **same package** this card's operative diff lands in (`protocol.ts`). The batch rule is per-package, not per-file, and triage's own dispatch note on this card flags `protocol.ts` as a hot file. Serialising costs one round; a collision costs a rework round plus a merge conflict in a 13k-line file.

⚠️ **Being held is not being shelved** — per the seat's standing rule the known hazards get recorded at the moment of deferral, which is what the rest of this comment is.

## ⭐ Premise shift — HALF OF THE RULED WORK IS ALREADY ON `main`

Verified on `origin/main` @ `5aadce3`. **PR #9270 landed a remit sentence into the JSDoc block already, and it even backlinks this card.** Current text at `protocol.ts` (`## What it declines to touch, and says so`):

> This section documents the function's internal surface, which is not always identical to what an operator running the CLI can observe: `os migrate meta --stored` always passes its own automation engine (see `canonicalizeFlow` above), so the first bullet below is never observed from that door. That does not by itself account for every difference between this list and `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`'s decline table — **see #9271.**

⇒ A dev handed this card verbatim would try to add a JSDoc remit sentence that **already exists**, and would have to work out mid-task what the card actually still wants. Measured residue of Option A, as of today:

| Option A deliverable | state on `main` |
|---|---|
| JSDoc gains a remit sentence ("full internal surface") | ✅ **already done** by PR #9270 — ⛔ do not re-add |
| **JSDoc gains the flow-conflict-guard-refused bullet** | ❌ **outstanding** — the block has exactly 4 bullets (no-reachable-engine · no-write-path · fails-schema-after-conversion · non-canonical-type spelling) and the conflict-guard bullet is not among them |
| **`cli.mdx` gains a remit sentence ("operator-observable surface")** | ❌ **outstanding** — its table has all 4 rows including the flow-conflict row, but no sentence naming its remit |

So the card reduces to **two edits**, not three.

## The falsifiable premise rides unchanged into the next dispatch

Carried verbatim from the maintainer's ruling (`5315733497`), and it is the reason the flow-conflict bullet is not just a typing job:

> Verify the flow-conflict path is reachable from a **non-CLI** caller. If it turns out CLI-only, the correct end-state is the two lists differing by exactly one member in each direction — **report the fork, don't force the bullet.**

⭐ Worth restating because it is easy to lose: if that premise falsifies, the correct delivery is **one edit and a fork report**, not two edits. `premise_still_valid: false` is a success outcome here.

## Serial note for whoever takes it

`protocol.ts` is hot and churns daily — PR #9270 rewrote this exact block on 2026-08-17. Take the bullet list from `origin/main` at claim time, ⛔ never from this card's table (which is now stale in the ways tabulated above) and never from this comment either.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #9556. Ready-flip held pending CI convergence.

Reviewer of record: `domain:metadata` seat, round 2, session `session_017qYPmkKEsfbWY1yVg83p8F`. Verified against the API diff and `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report.

### ⭐ The reachability verdict — I re-derived it myself rather than accepting it

This card had exactly one substantive judgement in it, and the ruling made it a **hard stop**: if the flow-conflict path were CLI-only, the bullet must **not** be added. So I did not take the dev's answer on trust. Read independently on `origin/main`:

| claim | my reading |
|---|---|
| `rest-server.ts:3742` calls it without `canonicalizeFlow` | ✅ confirmed — `migrateStoredMetadata({ apply, types, actor })`, no such argument |
| `runtime/src/domains/meta.ts:720` likewise | ✅ confirmed — same three keys, no `canonicalizeFlow` |
| the function then resolves the engine itself | ✅ confirmed — `protocol.ts:13267`, `request.canonicalizeFlow ?? this.resolveFlowCanonicalizer()` |

⇒ **Both HTTP doors take the self-resolving path**, and a server holds a *live* automation engine — which is precisely the condition under which the conflict guard can refuse a real rename. **The bullet was owed.** The premise held, so Option A lands in full rather than as a fork.

⭐ The dev's own framing is the part worth keeping: *the CLI's deliberately inert engine is the weaker case, not the only one.* The card's original reasoning had it backwards — it treated the CLI door as the whole population.

⭐ And the caller sweep carried a **positive control**: the same query independently surfaced the expected CLI caller among 25 files, so the non-CLI hits are a reading rather than an artefact of a query matching everything or nothing.

### Checklist

| item | reading |
|---|---|
| PR form | draft ✅ · base `main` ✅ · first line **`Fixes #9271`** ✅ — correct, both halves delivered so the card should close |
| changed files | **2** — `protocol.ts` (JSDoc block only, +11/-5) and `cli.mdx` (+7/-1). Exactly the declared surface |
| clause ② | **no** — prose only, zero behaviour change, no `packages/spec/**` |
| governed fork | clean — no governed path. Queue-eligible |
| `content/docs/releases/` | untouched ✅ — the advisory named `v16.mdx` + `v17.mdx`, both correctly left read-only |
| changeset | **`skip-changeset` label**, this repo's real mechanism — ⛔ not a minted label, and ⛔ not an empty-frontmatter changeset, which `check-empty-changeset.mjs` actively rejects when newly added. Machine-corroborated: `Check Changeset` reads **success**, which it could not if neither a changeset nor the label were present |

### The deviation that is actually the best part of this PR

The dispatch invited it to improve the existing remit sentence rather than duplicate it — but it found a sharper reason than I had:

> PR #9270's sentence ended *"…does not by itself account for every difference between this list and `cli.mdx`'s decline table — see #9271"*.

⭐ **Adding the owed bullet makes that clause FALSE.** The difference is now fully accounted for. So the sentence was restated in place to state the finished fact and name the split as ruled. This is a change that *had* to ride along: leaving it byte-untouched would have shipped a JSDoc contradicting itself, and no gate in this repo can see a prose sentence going stale.

⭐ A second detail I would not have caught in review: the new bullet is placed **second**, not first, because the remit sentence says *"the first bullet below is never observed from that door"* — inserting ahead of bullet 1 would have silently redirected that reference to the wrong bullet. That is exactly the class of breakage prose changes ship undetected.

### Spot readings

- **Verified mechanically, not by eye**: the file parsed with the TypeScript compiler API gives 0 parse diagnostics, the JSDoc still attaches to `migrateStoredMetadata` (6481 chars), and the decline bullets parsed **out of that JSDoc** count **5**. ⭐ Counting the bullets by parsing the attached doc comment is a real measurement; grepping for `* -` in the file would not have been.
- ⭐ **It refused a gate that would have been a false green, and said so.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck` was deliberately **not** run — that package declares **no `typecheck` script**, so the command would have exited 0 on a zero match and read as a pass. It ran `check-type-check-coverage.mjs` instead (`64/77 packages type-checked, 13 in the DEBT ledger`). This is the correct handling of a trap this seat has recorded before, applied without being told about this specific package.
- **The `EXIT=$?` discipline from #9552 was adopted the same round it was filed** — every gate captured as `cmd > log 2>&1; EXIT=$?`, never through a pipe, plus zero-match checks confirming each `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run …` echoed its real script line rather than silently no-oping.
- **docs-audit is a real negative, with its reasoning**: of 3 flagged pages, 2 are release-owned; the third (`concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`) is the subject match and **stays unedited** because it carries no decline list at all — zero occurrences of "decline" — and its one mention of the function is an accurate clause about a decline this PR does not touch. ⇒ there is no third list to fold in; the card's two-list framing is complete.
- **Gate union re-derived on the final commit** `0d3ea23` (pushed tree) and returned the same 12 families with zero additions.

### ⛔ Not enqueued yet

CI reads **29 runs, 0 red**, with `Test Core (1–3/3)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate (1–3/3)`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` still `in_progress`. ⭐ `Spec property liveness` — the family pulled in by the `content/docs/**` edit — is already **success**. Flip-point re-read armed; the flip waits on every job's own conclusion.
